recognize_zh: 周邊血抹片中一顆與中性球大小相近的細胞，細胞內佈滿粗大、深紫黑色的顆粒，覆蓋在核上使核輪廓幾乎看不清，這是嗜鹼性球（basophil）最典型的辨識線索。
features: Cell slightly larger than a red cell, similar in size to a neutrophil
Numerous coarse, dark purple-black granules distributed over the cytoplasm and nucleus
Nuclear outline largely obscured by overlying granules
Granules extend to the cell periphery giving a slightly irregular border
Background red cells show fine dark dots, most likely a staining/drying artifact
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a single basophil with abundant coarse, dark purple-black granules that overlie and obscure the nucleus and extend to the cell margin. The surrounding red cells are normocytic with fine dark dots that most likely represent a preparation artifact. No blasts or other abnormal leukocytes are present in the field. Findings are consistent with a normal basophil.

ddx.vs: Mast cells are larger with a round central nucleus that remains visible and are rarely seen in blood outside systemic mastocytosis or mast cell leukemia.
Toxic granulation consists of dark granules in a neutrophil whose lobated nucleus remains clearly visible, often with Döhle bodies or vacuoles.
Eosinophils contain uniform refractile orange-red granules with a visible bilobed nucleus rather than dark purple-black granules obscuring the nucleus.
